extracted.intended_audience: Researchers preparing manuscripts for submission to Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and standards for preparing, formatting, depositing data, disclosing conflicts, and submitting Research Reports, Commentaries, Perspectives, and Colloquium Papers to PNAS, including track-specific review requirements and production/formatting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope / article types
rubrics_metrics.description: PNAS publishes research reports, commentaries, perspectives, and colloquium papers. PNAS is a general science journal with a broad scientific audience. All papers should be intelligible to this audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research Reports describe original research of exceptional importance. Commentaries and Perspectives are by invitation. Colloquium Papers report Academy colloquia. Frame content for a broad scientific readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track I — Communicated manuscripts (member-communicated)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Academy member may 'communicate' manuscripts for others; prior to submission the member obtains outside reviews from at least two qualified referees, each from a different institution and not from the authors’ institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include names/contact info (including e-mails) of referees, the reviews on the PNAS review form, and the authors' responses. The communicating member should include a brief statement endorsing publication in PNAS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track II — Direct submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors (members and nonmembers) may submit directly to the PNAS office; in cover letter or online form authors must recommend up to 3 appropriate Editorial Board members, 3 NAS members expert in the area, and 5 qualified referees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Editorial Board may choose an editor not on that list or reject without further review. The editor conducts review as described for Track I. The editor's name (may be anonymous until acceptance) will be published as the editor of the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track III — Member-contributed manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: An Academy member may submit his/her own manuscripts; submissions must be accompanied by names/contact information (including e-mail) of knowledgeable colleagues who reviewed the paper, the reviews on the PNAS review form, the authors' response, and a brief statement endorsing publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Academy member must be a corresponding author on the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Board evaluation and resubmission restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: All Tracks are evaluated by the Editorial Board, which may reject manuscripts without further review or subject them to review and reject those that do not meet journal standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts rejected by one member cannot be resubmitted through another member. When revisions are requested prior to final decision, revised papers must be received within three months or will be treated as new submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No prior or simultaneous publication / related submissions disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles are accepted provided they have not been published previously or concurrently submitted elsewhere. Related manuscripts that are in press or submitted elsewhere must be included with your PNAS submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify any related submitted or in-press manuscripts when submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for previously published figures/tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures or tables that have been published elsewhere must be identified, and permission of the copyright holder for both the print and the online editions must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See sample permission request letter at the PNAS permissions resource.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship eligibility and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorship should be limited to those who have contributed substantially to the work. The corresponding author must have obtained permission from all authors for submission of each version and for any change in authorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit authorship to substantive contributors; ensure all authors consent to submission and any authorship changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coauthor responsibilities and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: All collaborators share some degree of responsibility for any paper they coauthor. Coauthors accountable for the integrity of the data include those who carry out analysis, write the manuscript, present major findings, or provide scientific leadership. Others with limited contributions are responsible for their parts but may have limited responsibility for other results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All collaborators should have an appropriate process for reviewing the accuracy of reported results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author contribution footnote requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must indicate their specific contributions to the published work; this information will be posted online as a footnote to the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Designed research; Performed research; Contributed new reagents or analytic tools; Analyzed data; Wrote the paper. Authors may list multiple contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest disclosure and funding acknowledgments
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors, members, referees, and editors must disclose any association that poses a Conflict of Interest in connection with the manuscript. Authors must acknowledge all funding sources supporting the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See PNAS COI web page for details; include disclosure statements with submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: A completed form assigning Copyright to the National Academy of Sciences must be returned to the PNAS office before the paper can be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This and other required forms are available on the PNAS website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo policy and press coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Academy may distribute embargoed copies of an accepted article to the press prior to publication; embargoes expire at 5:00 PM Eastern time, the Monday before publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may freely talk with the press but should coordinate with the PNAS News Office so reporters are aware of PNAS policy. If presenting an embargoed paper at a conference before publication, contact the PNAS News Office immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human and animal subjects approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Research involving Human and Animal Subjects must have been approved by the author’s institutional review board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All clinical investigation must have been conducted according to the principles expressed in the Declaration of Helsinki.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recombinant DNA containment compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: For research using Recombinant DNA, physical and biological containment must conform to National Institutes of Health guidelines or those of a corresponding agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NIH or corresponding national agency containment guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique materials availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must make Unique Materials (e.g., cloned DNAs; antibodies; bacterial, animal, or plant cells; viruses; and computer programs) promptly available on request by qualified researchers for their own use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply will preclude future publication in the journal. Authors may charge a modest amount to cover costs. Contact PNAS if difficulty obtaining materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Database deposition and accession codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Accession codes must be supplied for publication. A footnote indicating that the data have been deposited will be added to the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit nucleotide sequences to GenBank/EMBL/DDBJ and obtain an accession number before publication. Provide accession codes in the data deposition footnote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural data deposition (Protein Data Bank / NDB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of papers describing new structure determinations must submit to the Protein Data Bank (or equivalent) all structural data required to validate the discussion, including x-ray amplitudes and derived atomic coordinates; for NMR include resonance assignments and all restraints and coordinates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles must include literature references for coordinate datasets and dataset identification. Authors must agree to release coordinates when the article is published.

rubrics_metrics.name: fMRI data deposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) studies should deposit data directly with the fMRI Data Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide deposition details and accession if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting Information (SI) policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting Information enhances papers by providing additional substantive material, but the print version of the paper must stand on its own merits. SI is reviewed along with the paper but is posted on the PNAS website instead of appearing in print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to SI in the manuscript at appropriate points. SI cannot be altered after acceptance. Editors may suggest moving material online to save journal space or if necessary for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable file formats and size limits for Supporting Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Word, WordPerfect, RTF (PDF acceptable for LaTeX) for text; figure legends in Word/WordPerfect/RTF; figure images JPEG, GIF, or PDF (do not embed numbers/legends/author names in image); tables Word, Excel, HTML, or PDF (one table per file); movies QuickTime (.mov) or MPEG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File sizes should not exceed 5 MB (images should not exceed 500 pixels per inch). Movies should be no more than 10 MB. Web pages: provide complete list of files and main page; acceptable formats include HTML, PDF, JPEG, GIF, plain text, and Excel.

rubrics_metrics.name: URLs and archival requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PNAS must be able to archive all content necessary for evaluation; links to web sites other than permanent public repositories are not acceptable. Links to authors’ home or university pages are not permitted and will be removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use public databases (GenBank, etc.) for archivable content. PNAS copyright assignment permits authors to post their PNAS paper and additional material on their home page after PNAS publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal cover figure specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are invited to submit scientifically interesting and visually arresting cover images; images should be original and copyright will transfer to PNAS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include brief lay-language caption (50–60 words) and credit information. Images should be 21.5 cm wide by 22.5 cm high, files .eps or .tif in CMYK mode. Provide manuscript number, author name, phone, and e-mail. Hard-copy prints: send two glossy prints labeled with top indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication charges — page, SI, color, open access
rubrics_metrics.description: Page charge of $70 per printed page will be assessed from all authors who have funds available. $200 per article assessed for Supporting Information. $300 per color figure or table; $150 per replacement/deletion of a color figure/table; additional $200 per color SI item requiring scanning. Open access surcharge $1,000 (or $750 with 2005 site license).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles are accepted/rejected solely on merit. Requests for waiver of charges should be submitted to pnas@nas.edu. All articles are free online after 6 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online submission and required file types
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors submitting directly (Track II) may submit PDFs of double-spaced papers via www.PNAScentral.org. Source files are required for all other submissions, including Track II revisions. Members submitting via Tracks I and III should also submit via the web.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online submission expedites editorial process and reduces mailing costs. If unable to submit online contact the PNAS office. Supporting Information may also be submitted online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital figure file formats and production quality
rubrics_metrics.description: TIFF and EPS for Macintosh or PC are the only acceptable formats for figures that will appear in the print journal. All color images must be in CMYK mode. Include font files for any text. PC or Macintosh Adobe PostScript fonts must be used (no system 'bitmap' fonts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Images must be final size, preferably 1 column (8.7 cm) width; figures wider than 1 column should be 10.5–18.0 cm. Numbers/letters/symbols should be at least 2 mm after reduction and consistent. Composite figures must be preassembled. See PNAS digital art guidelines for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table formatting and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Number tables (Arabic numerals) in the order cited in the text. Each table should have a brief title, be on a separate page, and be double-spaced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number supporting figures/tables to follow all figures and tables in main text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting Information referencing and print self-sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The print version of the paper must stand on its own without the Supporting Information. If detailed materials and methods are placed in SI, provide sufficient detail in the print edition methods to enable a reader to follow logic and reference the online methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a paper is fundamentally a study of a new method/technique, methods must be described completely in the print edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formats for SI images, tables, movies, and web pages
rubrics_metrics.description: For SI: images JPEG/GIF/PDF (do not save figure numbers/legends/author names as part of image); tables Word/Excel/HTML/PDF; movies QuickTime (.mov) or MPEG; web pages HTML/PDF/JPEG/GIF/plain text/Excel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a brief legend for each figure in Word/WordPerfect/RTF; include table title and legend in table file; do not use tabs/spaces to separate columns in Word tables; provide main page name and complete file list for web pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting print manuscripts (Tracks I and III) — copies and disks required
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit five complete copies of the manuscript in final form, pages numbered, plus one set of print-quality figures, four sets of review-quality figures, and one photocopied set of figures. Include manuscript text, digital art, and Supporting Information each on separate computer disks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify platform, program, first author, date, and file name on each disk label. Also include completed Copyright Assignment/Documentation Report Form, character count breakdown, disclosure of COI, acknowledgment of funding, classification, and references per PNAS style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text-on-disk requirement for print submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Print manuscripts must be accompanied by a computer disk containing the final text; the version on disk must match the hard copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines for TeX/LaTeX submissions are provided. Supporting Information should be on separate disks clearly marked 'Supporting Information for the Web' with title, corresponding author, file names, and program/version used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original figures and returns
rubrics_metrics.description: Original drawings, high-quality photographs, or laser prints are required (halftones should be high-quality originals or photographs). For color figures, submit one set of prints for the printer at final size and four sets of high-quality prints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label back of each figure with first author’s name, figure number, orientation (top), and desired final size. Return of figures cannot be guaranteed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript length and character-count formula
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum length of a research article is six printed pages or 47,000 characters, including all text, spaces, and characters displaced by figures, tables, and equations. The total character count equals: number of characters (including spaces) in the text (exclude tables) + converted character equivalents for figures, tables, spaces around figures/tables/equations, and equations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion rules specified: add height in cm of each figure multiplied by 180 for a one-column figure or 360 for a two-column figure; add height in number of lines of each table (60 for one-column or 120 for two-column); add 120-character allowance for space above and below each single column of a figure/table/equation; add 60 characters for each one-column line of equation. If your word processor character count excludes spaces, add the word count to obtain characters including spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript standard order of sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard order: title page, abstract, introduction, materials and methods, results, discussion, acknowledgments, references, figure legends, and tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow this order when preparing manuscript files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title guidance and length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles should be simple, informative, and comprehensible for a broad scientific audience. Avoid nonstandard abbreviations and colonic phrases. Titles may not be phrased as questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles are limited to three lines or 135 characters including spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page classification and metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Classification: select a major (Physical, Biological, or Social Sciences) and a minor category from the provided lists; dual classifications permitted and exceptional dual within major subject to Editorial Board approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also include author affiliation(s), corresponding author contact details, manuscript information (number of text pages, figures, tables), and word/character counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author affiliation and corresponding author information
rubrics_metrics.description: Include department, institution, and complete address for each author; use superscripts if different affiliations. Provide name, complete address, telephone, fax, and e-mail of corresponding author; mailing and e-mail addresses will appear in print and online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding author will handle proofs and correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript information and counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the number of text pages (including references and figure legends), number of figures, and number of tables. Provide word and character counts: number of words in abstract and total number of characters in paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These metadata are required on the title page or submission forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations footnote policy
rubrics_metrics.description: List nonstandard abbreviations used five or more times. Define these where first mentioned in the text and do not use them in the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an abbreviations footnote on the title page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data deposition footnote
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply all database accession numbers and/or codes in a data deposition footnote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This footnote will appear with the published article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract length and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an abstract of no more than 250 words on page 2 of the manuscript. Abstracts should explain to the general reader the major contributions of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References in the abstract must be cited in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods placement and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe procedures in sufficient detail so that the work can be repeated. Methods must be presented before Results and Discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If detailed methods are placed in SI, include enough detail in print methods to enable readers to follow logic and reference the online methods. For papers fundamentally about new methods, describe them completely in the print edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language, nomenclature, and units
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow spelling and usage given in Webster’s Third New International Dictionary or the Random House Dictionary. Avoid laboratory jargon. Use correct chemical names, specify strains of organisms, and identify trade names with initial capital letter then lowercase. Use SI units and symbols whenever possible; when SI units are not used, provide conversion factor on first usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide names/addresses of suppliers for uncommon reagents or instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote symbol order
rubrics_metrics.description: Use symbols in the order: *, †, ‡, §, ¶, ||, **, ††, ‡‡, §§, ¶¶.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow this ordering for symbol footnotes in the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgments content
rubrics_metrics.description: List dedications, acknowledgments, and funding sources in the Acknowledgments section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include grant numbers and funding agencies as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: References — eligibility and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: References must be in PNAS style. Only published or in-press papers and books may be cited; abstracts presented at meetings are not permitted. References should be cited in numerical order as they appear in text. All authors (unless 10 or more) should be named; if 10 or more, list first 10 followed by et al.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because tables/figures are inserted where first cited, number references accordingly. Databases are cited in the text or as footnotes. Corresponding author must be prepared to provide a signed authorization for citation of unpublished data and personal communications. Use CASSI for journal title abbreviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure legends separate from figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide figure legends separately from the figure images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include legends in the manuscript file where indicated, not embedded in image files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomenclature and style standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Use international standards on nomenclature. For recommended style guides, nomenclature, abbreviations, and symbols, consult the PNAS website or contact the PNAS office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow field-specific international conventions for naming and symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updates and checking the latest guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The PNAS Information for Authors is published in the first print issue of the year and is available online; check the web site for the latest version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consult the website to ensure compliance with the most recent requirements.
